newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: The Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Athinais P loading 19,200 tonnes soymeal. Hsing May loading 54,000 tonnes soybeans/meal. Decurion loading 31,000 tonnes soybeans. Aghia Markella loading 51,698 tonnes soybeans/meal. Waiting to dock, seven vessels to load soymeal and two for soybeans.
Road: 1,315 trucks carrying soybeans arrived on May 28 and 29, 715 trucks with soymeal and 119 with vegetable oils, including soyoil.

Loading: 68,797 tonnes soybeans, 37,330 tonnes soymeal. NOTE: Rain slowed the loading of grains at the port terminal but loading was three days ahead of schedule, reducing the impact of the delay, a spokeswoman said.

Vessels: At public terminal, Lake Avery loading 29,000 tonnes soybeans. Waiting to dock, Gina Iuliano to load 53,550 tonnes soybeans and Panli to load 36,550 tonnes soybeans. At Cargill private terminal, Petimata Ot Rms loading 31,000 tonnes soymeal. Waiting to dock, Lika to load 60,000 tonnes soybeans and Stanford Trader to load 16,000 tonnes soybeans.
Road: 118 trucks carrying 3,128 tonnes soybeans arrived on May 29 as well as 18 trucks with 492 tonnes soymeal.
Rail: 76 wagons arrived carrying 4,970 tonnes soybeans.
Stocks: 109,964 tonnes soybeans, 20,838 tonnes soymeal. NOTE: Heavy rains slowed loading of grains Thursday and Friday.
